elements.sub: The shape of curves and thrown stones

elements.text: When you kick a football, its path through the air forms a curve called a parabola. That curve is governed by a quadratic equation!
Highest power of x is 2. The coefficient 'a' cannot be 0, otherwise it collapses into a linear equation.

D > 0: Two distinct real roots
D = 0: Two equal roots
D < 0: No real roots
The Quadratic Formula works every single time — even when middle-term splitting fails!
Calculate D first to check if solutions exist, then apply the formula. Tap ✋ to ask any doubt!

beats.narration: Welcome! Whenever you toss a basketball or launch a rocket, its path arcs through the sky in a curve called a parabola. To find when that ball hits the ground, you solve a Quadratic Equation. Let's master it right now.

Every quadratic equation can be arranged into standard form: a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero. Notice the condition: 'a' can never be zero. If 'a' were zero, the x squared term vanishes and it turns into a simple linear equation.

Before solving, always calculate the Discriminant D: b squared minus 4 a c. It tells you the nature of roots in advance. If D is positive, you get two distinct real solutions. If D is zero, exactly one repeated root. If D is negative, no real roots exist.

And here is the legendary Quadratic Formula: x equals minus b plus or minus square root of D, all divided by 2 a. While factoring by splitting the middle term can get tricky with decimals or square roots, this formula never fails.

To recap: arrange your equation into a x squared plus b x plus c equals 0, compute D equals b squared minus 4 a c, and plug into the formula. If you ever get stuck or have a question, hit the raise hand button and ask me live!
